name: from_non_null_in
declaration: unsafe fn from_non_null_in (raw : NonNull < T > , alloc : A) -> Self
rules: `raw` must point to a block of memory allocated by `alloc`.
For a non-zero-sized `T`, the allocation pointed to by `raw` must have the layout `Layout::for_value(&*raw.as_ptr())`, as required by `Box<T, A>`.
For a zero-sized `T`, `raw` must be non-null and sufficiently aligned for `T`.
`raw` must point to a valid value of `T`.

Calling `Box::from_non_null_in(raw, alloc)` transfers ownership of the pointer to the resulting `Box`; the caller must not create duplicate ownership that would cause a double-free, including by calling this function twice on the same allocation.
